messages:
anya: Heads-up — I ran the p95-driven batching experiment idea this morning for Route-Tier mapping. Trying to push dynamic token budgets per route instead of global token caps. Preliminary observations below, want quick sync before we run a canary.

mike: Nice — can you summarize config and perf numbers?

anya: Config: microbatcher with continuous batching enabled, queue-policy=latency-slo, token-budgeter=dynamic-by-route. Targets: p95 <= 120ms for interactive routes (tier=prod-interactive), p95 <= 250ms for background routes (tier=batch). Kernel policy: prefer flash-attn-quantized on short-seq, fallback to gemm-int8 for long seq. KV cache: prefix-only caching enabled.

sofia: Quick note: KV hit ratio dropped ~6% on prod-interactive under the dynamic split. Could be because token-budgeting moved more short requests into separate microbatches so cache locality changed.

anya: Exactly — hit ratio went from 86% -> 80% on the p95 experiment window. That's consistent with more aggressive token slicing.

mike: What were the p95 numbers?

anya: Baseline (static 64-token cap global): prod-interactive p95=135ms, batch p95=210ms. After dynamic budgets: prod-interactive p95=118ms, batch p95=245ms. Overall cost/tokens increased ~3% due to fewer KV hits and smaller microbatch amortization.

sam: So we hit the interactive p95 SLO but regressed batch slightly. Is that acceptable? Also how did GPU utilization change?

anya: GPU util steady +2% (more frequent kernel swaps, slightly lower occupancy on some units). Cost trade-off: better tail for latency-sensitive routes, small throughput hit for low-priority routes.

sofia: I dug into profiler samples. Main regressions show increased kernel-launch frequency: short sequences end up on flash-attn kernel but we see more kernel fallback thrash when sequence length fluctuates near the switch threshold.

mike: Can you paste the profiler snippet?

anya: Sure:
```
# perf summary (10k requests sample)
route=prod-interactive: p50=45ms p95=118ms p99=230ms
route=batch: p50=180ms p95=245ms p99=420ms
KV hit ratio: 86% -> 80% (interactive)
Kernel switches per request: 0.12 -> 0.28
Average microbatch size: 5.8 -> 3.4
```

sofia: That kernel-switches metric is the smoking gun. Each fallback adds ~6-12ms median overhead and increases variance.

mike: Could we smooth the kernel selection boundary? Like hysteresis or sequence-length windowing to avoid flip-flopping?

anya: I tried a quick hysteresis: only change kernel if observed seq_len mean crosses threshold by 12 tokens over last 50 requests. That cut kernel-switches per request to 0.08 and raised p50 by 3ms but reduced p95 jitter.

sam: Sounds promising. Any effect on KV?

anya: Slight improvement — KV hit ratio recovered 2 points (to ~82%). Microbatch size stayed low (~3.7) though.

sofia: Two more ideas: 1) allow token-budgets to allocate a small reserved prefix budget to keep cache locality (like reserve 1-2 tokens per request to increase prefix reuse), 2) route-aware batch merging: if two interactive requests arrive within 10ms and have similar seq_len, merge them even if token budgets are conservative.

mike: Both seem reasonable. We need safe knobs for canary. What's the exact canary plan?

sam: Propose: roll to 5% of prod nodes for 6 hours with these delta flags: hysteresis=12, window=50, reserved_prefix_tokens=1, route_merge_window_ms=10. Monitor p95/p99, KV-hit, kernel-switches, and GPU util. If p95 degrades for batch>5% or kernel-switches >0.2 -> rollback.

anya: I'll push the canary config. Deploy-bot will run the rollout.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: canary group "slo-batcher-tokengrid-canary" targeting 5% of prod nodes. CI passed: unit+integration tests. Estimated start 10:30 PST.

mike: Also add a small probe that logs sequence-length histogram per route at 1m granularity so we can refine the hysteresis threshold post-canary.

sofia: Agreed. Add a kv-hit slice by prefix-length too.

anya: Will add probes and the canary flags now. Planning to run 6h then collect profiles and upload to shared perf bucket.

sam: After canary, if stable, schedule a wider rollout but with a gradual token-budget scaling so batch tier gets incremental budget increase to avoid sudden throughput drops.

anya: Thanks all — I'll post the canary link and the results snapshot when done. cc @mike @sofia @sam
